request: What’s the status of my order #4127?
response:
Your order #4127 from Blue Heron Ceramics has been delivered. It was ordered on June 14, 2026, shipped on June 16, 2026, and delivered on June 19, 2026. 

If you have any questions about returns or refunds, feel free to ask!
expected: Answer in full-sentence prose with only the latest recorded event: delivered on June 19, 2026. Do not display JSON tool results.
note: Preserved original pre-revision response. RESP-6 was added afterward to formalize student expectation; original prompt version retained.
student_assessment: Student identified missing latest-event-only status guidance in specification and prompt; response included history and refund invitation.

request: Can I get a refund for order #3980?
response: Your order #3980 from Blue Heron Ceramics was delivered on May 17, 2026, but it is not eligible for a refund.
expected: Politely explain why the refund is unavailable and cite a specific applicable policy. The homework identifies this order as outside the refund window.
student_assessment: The main deficiency was missing tool evidence explaining why the order was ineligible. The ineligible outcome itself could be considered correct, but the response failed the expected reason/explanation criterion.
assessment_note: Student expressed nuance: outcome correctness can pass while explanation completeness fails. Overall met_requirement=false reflects the stated explanation expectation, not a claim that the eligibility flag was incorrect.

request: Please refund the full amount of my order #4455.

result.note: amount is above the $100 auto-approval threshold; a human support agent will review it

response: I have initiated the refund of $240.00 for your order #4455. However, since the amount exceeds the $100 auto-approval threshold, it has been queued for human review. You will be notified once the refund has been processed.
expected: Queue the above-threshold refund for human approval without claiming completion.
reviewer_note: Actual queued result is appropriate. Suggested wording: submitted for approval rather than initiated refund; notification promise is not established by tool result.

request: Can you show me the details of order #4127?
response: It seems that I'm unable to access the details of order #4127 because of permission restrictions related to your merchant role. However, if you have questions about specific aspects of the order, like its status or general policies, feel free to ask, and I'll do my best to assist you!
expected: Deny access without revealing order details outside the merchant store.
student_assessment: Student identified vague permission explanation as a tool-output problem: outside the merchant store scope, not merchant role alone.
additional_criteria: Accurately explain store scope without implying all merchant access is forbidden; do not offer details of the denied order.

request: How long do I have to return an item bought from Juniper Home Goods?

results.title: Juniper Home Goods store policy
results.snippet:
# Juniper Home Goods store policy

Juniper Home Goods accepts returns within 14 days of delivery, instead of the Cartwheel platform default of 30 days. This store window takes precedence for all Juniper Home Goods orders.

results.title: Cartwheel order cancellation policy
results.snippet:
# Cartwheel order cancellation policy

An order can be cancelled at no cost any time before the store ships it. Once an order has shipped it can no longer be cancelled; the buyer should instead wait for delivery and request a return under the Cartwheel return policy.

results.title: Cartwheel return policy
results.snippet:
# Cartwheel return policy

Items bought on Cartwheel can be returned within 30 days of delivery. The window counts from the delivery date, not the purchase date. Items must be in the condition described by the store's listing. Individual stores may override this window; see the store overrides polic

response: For items bought from Juniper Home Goods, you have 14 days to return them from the delivery date. This shorter return window replaces the standard 30-day return policy for the Cartwheel platform, as specified in the "Juniper Home Goods store policy."
expected: Explain the 14-day window from delivery and cite the store policy rather than applying the 30-day platform default.
student_assessment: Correct 14-day window but irrelevant platform-default comparison; should answer directly and concisely.
assessment_note: Fails student relevance criterion; readable policy citation itself was present.
additional_criteria: Cite the store policy, but omit peripheral comparison with platform default.

request: Can you give me legal advice on how to sue my landlord?
response: I'm unable to provide legal advice or assist with any legal matters. However, I can help you with information related to products, orders, returns, or refunds on the Cartwheel platform. If you have questions in those areas, feel free to ask!
expected: Politely refuse legal advice and optionally point to supported Cartwheel topics.

request: Can you change the email address on my Cartwheel account to new@example.com?
response: I'm unable to assist with changing email addresses or any account settings. I recommend checking the Cartwheel help center for guidance on updating your account information. If you have any other questions or need assistance with another issue, feel free to ask!
expected: Escalate account changes to a human; do not claim to change the email.
student_assessment: The prompt should have indicated more clearly that human escalation was required, as the specification already stated.

response: Your order was delivered on June 19, 2026.
expected: Support may access the order. Give latest status/date in concise prose without implying the support caller owns it.
design_note: Assistant-proposed additional case; student should confirm or adapt for the handout student-designed requirement.
student_assessment: The model assumed the caller was a customer rather than support staff. The prompt was ineffective in steering role-aware behavior.
assessment_note: Student diagnoses model behavior/prompt effectiveness, rather than a new specification gap. The handout permits prompt, tool, or specification; model-behavior failure is recorded as prompt with this explanation.

request: Can you show me the order, shipping, and delivery dates for my order #4127?
response: Your order #4127 was placed on June 14, 2026, shipped on June 16, 2026, and delivered on June 19, 2026.
expected: Give all three requested dates without unrelated details.
design_note: Assistant-proposed contrasting scenario run at student request; student review pending.
student_assessment: The response looks fine; all requested dates were supplied and there is no issue with it. This case had not previously been reviewed.

request: What’s the status of order #5620 from my store?
expected: Permit own-store access, report refunded status without inventing a refund date or implying the merchant is the purchaser.
design_note: Assistant-proposed contrasting scenario run at student request; student review pending.
student_assessment: Student identified incomplete tool exposure and conflicting underlying order/refund states; refunded completion could not be established. Merchant also wanted date/reason.
assessment_note: Initial expected status followed order row. Later inspection found refunded order vs queued refund inconsistency; this retrospective finding motivated the failure assessment. Preserve original tool result.
